revisits.note: S2.1 audit-fix (Optimizer/docs/sonnet-correction-20260725-katachi-interior-growth-s2-1-audit-fixes.md). Independent audit found default rootTarget=5 produced a 3-4-component STL the old save gate silently accepted, a score-term scale mismatch (coverage gain ~0.0005-0.002 vs material penalty ~0.116), and legacy S2 recipes silently passing through unmigrated. Fixed C1-C6 in the required order: C1 removed independent extra-root creation (graph root always 1 now, rootTarget is a documented no-op, new plateContactCount metric, evaluateSaveGate now fails connectedComponents!==1); C2 unified support-angle math into one shared allowedLateralForStepMm helper and found a real bug in the process -- the old colonizeTiltRad computed max tilt as angle-margin (~27deg at default 30deg) when rule 5's own formula gives 90-angle-margin (~57deg), verified numerically at 6 angles -- plus route-level (not single-continuous-formula) cone integration and a new negative-rise-rejected rule; C3 added per-region RegionRouteState so plate-walk chains actually advance (root->child1->child2->...) instead of repeatedly re-selecting the same lowest unit; C4 added two-stage direct-gain-over-route-progress candidate selection and renormalized coverage-gain against a local search-area denominator instead of the whole host; C5 fixed S2.1 detection to use algorithmVersion's own absence (not primaryPathUnitIds, which S2-era results already had) with nullable diagnostic fields for legacy results and a per-result scoreWeights snapshot instead of reading the current global constant; C6 removed a vacuous always-true test assertion and kept the C1 regression test at default rootTarget rather than weakening it to 1. C7 (Worker offload/progress/cancel) NOT attempted (time-constrained, honest gap). Re-measured 27-row matrix: sphere/waisted improved substantially (sphere ring 75% coverage 8.75%->13.57%(ish)/19.42%), box coin/ring plateau early at a low value regardless of target after losing its extra roots. Minimum-pass gate (coin target 25% >=23% on all of box/sphere/waisted) remains UNMET (2.85%/6.40%/6.98%) -- reported honestly, not claimed as done. Real-browser verification found a genuine new issue: a ring-constrained candidate's save buttons were correctly disabled with connectedComponents=8 despite rootCount=1 -- graph connectivity was fine but mesh-level smooth-min fusion wasn't, exactly the kind of case C1's gate fix is meant to catch. Tests grew from 60 to 64 (all pass); partition suite (102) unchanged. Not committed; not staged; not pushed; not deployed (author review pending).

S2.1 coverage attainment (Optimizer/docs/sonnet-instruction-20260725-katachi-interior-growth-s2-1-coverage-attainment.md). NOT COMPLETE per the instruction's own §7.1 minimum-pass matrix (target 25% must reach >=23% on all of box/sphere/waisted for coin-constrained; actual measured after this round: box 3.77%, sphere 5.57%, waisted 4.53% -- roughly 5-6x short) -- reported honestly as unmet, not claimed as done. Real, tested algorithmic work landed: (1) a genuine bug fix found while re-deriving the heading-tilt math for this round -- the S2-round colonizeTiltRad computed the max valid tilt-from-buildAxis as supportThresholdAngleDeg-margin (~27deg at the default 30deg) when rule 5's own formula (allowedLateral=verticalRise/tan(angle)) actually permits up to 90-angleDeg-margin (~57deg) -- verified numerically at 6 angles before relying on it, roughly doubling the previously-unused support cone; (2) new colonization.ts module: deterministic region grouping of the 4000 reference samples into ~14-sample grid cells with build-axis height-band quotas (computeSurfaceRegions), a reachability-cone pre-filter reusing rule 5's own cap (coneReachable), a self-contained uniform-grid SpatialHash, and an incremental marginal-coverage-gain estimator (estimateMarginalGain) used ONLY for search/scoring -- the final saved measuredSurfaceCoverage is always coverage.ts's canonical computeSurfaceCoverage, verified via an incrementalFinalDrift field that stayed exactly 0 across every test run; (3) growth.ts's growSurfaceColonization rewritten around three heading modes (approach/spread/plate-walk) and a multi-term candidate score (computeCandidateScore: coverage gain minus weighted material-cost/constraint-margin-risk/covered-overlap/path-length/host-boundary-risk, all Study-constant weights, never author-exposed) that evaluates every accepted candidate in a step-fraction tier and keeps the highest-scoring one instead of the first; plate-walk (near-horizontal, small-rise steps chained from the network's own lowest existing unit toward a cone-infeasible target's azimuth) widens the build-plate-supported base using ONLY the existing parent-contact rule (rule 4), so graph and mesh connectivity hold by construction, never a separate disconnected part (verified: single connectedComponents after S2.1 growth in a rootTarget:1 fixture). A budget increase (SAFETY_FACTOR 1.5->4, HARD_CAP 500->1200) was tried and measured to raise box-coin-25% to 8.52%, but pushed a full 3-candidate generateCandidates() call to ~77s, directly violating the instruction's own explicit §13 prohibition ('do not make the main thread block any longer') since Gate D (Worker offload) was not solved this round -- reverted back to 1.5/500. Diagnosed dominant limiting factor (measured, not guessed): 50-70% of accepted units are zero-coverage-gain 'approach' steps spent traveling through interior space toward a distant region before any material is close enough to register coverage -- with ~180-290 small regions per host and a mesh-generation-performance-capped budget in the low hundreds, only a handful of regions can be fully approached and completed per run; considered widening the incremental-gain search radius to credit approach paths that pass near OTHER regions, but reasoned (and did not implement, given convex hosts like box/sphere keep most of an interior approach path far from ANY surface sample until near the destination) that this reflects a real physical constraint on how support material reaches distant surface area, not a fixable search inefficiency. Gate D (staged timing, Worker offload, progress UI, cancel) was NOT attempted this round -- an honest, disclosed gap, not hidden. Tests: growth.test.ts grew from 50 to 60 assertions (10 new: SpatialHash-vs-brute-force match, incremental-vs-canonical drift bound, region-id determinism, coneReachable boundary-formula verification at 6 angles, two computeCandidateScore ordering tests, region-selection determinism across repeated same-seed runs, single-connected-component after S2.1 growth, and an algorithm-version/diagnostics-exposure check) -- all 60 pass, and all 50 pre-existing S1/S2-round tests pass unchanged, confirming no regression to Phase A invariance, reachability, determinism, or honest-gap reporting. Explicitly did NOT complete: §8's remaining ~10 test items (notably a literal frontier priority-queue class -- this design uses a deterministic region-priority scan instead, tested for determinism but not FIFO/heap semantics -- and full recipe/history.ts wiring of algorithmVersion/scoreWeights/coverageCurve, though those already surface via GrowthMetrics/CandidateProvenance), Gate D UI/Worker work, and did not touch coverage.ts's measurement definition, sample count/resolution/seed, the 2-percentage-point tolerance, Phase A's own primary-path search, or the Field/Coin/Ring comparison axis (all explicit §3 invariants, held). Never asserted support-free/printable/safe/load-bearing. Not committed; not staged; not pushed; not deployed (author review pending, per the instruction's own explicit no-deploy-this-round directive).

Support Backbone + Surface Colonization S1+S2 (Optimizer/docs/katachi-interior-growth-surface-coverage-plan-20260725.md): S1 = area-weighted surface-coverage MEASUREMENT (new coverage.ts, fixed reference mesh built once from hostSdf, fixed-N=4000 seeded CDF sampling, kind-aware covered test: coin=raw point-sphere union, ring=tapered-capsule union along the closed node chain so tube coverage isn't under-counted by raw spheres but ring holes still aren't over-counted by a global blend; reachable-unit-id set computed once, samples classified covered/no-material/unreachable, denominator never shrunk). S2 = coverage-directed colonization replacing Phase 1A/Stage 1A.1's undirected branch/fill entirely (Phase A's primary path untouched). DISCOVERED DURING THIS ROUND: a second, independent implementation of the same S1 design (surfaceCoverage.ts/surfaceCoverage.test.ts/measureS1.ts, apparently by a different concurrent agent/process given the antigravity-report-* filename measureS1.ts writes) already present in the same directory with near-identical timestamps -- consulted `codex exec` directly (non-interactive CLI call) for a design-reconciliation verdict rather than unilaterally picking one; adopted its fixed-N/seeded-CDF sampling recommendation and its correctly-flagged smooth-min-blend-leakage bug report, while it in turn confirmed my raw-sphere approach's under-counting of ring tube coverage -- coverage.ts was rewritten to fix both. The other implementation's files were left in place (not deleted; not mine to remove) -- see README Next. Six real bugs found and fixed in growSurfaceColonization via direct measurement, not guessed (full detail in growth.ts's own header comment above the function): (1) direct-line-to-target heading routinely violated rule 5's tan(supportThresholdAngleDeg) lateral:vertical cap once a target sat mostly sideways from the parent -- fixed by reusing Phase A's own bounded-tilt-from-buildAxis heading construction with only the AZIMUTH aimed at the target; (2) re-picking 'farthest uncovered' every iteration let the target oscillate between comparably-far regions before any single one was ever reached -- fixed with target COMMITMENT across iterations; (3) Phase A's own autoBudget.totalBudget (sized for a primary path, not a coverage fraction) silently capped every run under 10% regardless of target -- colonization now gets its own larger, coverage-area-derived budget; (4) aiming a candidate's center at a raw host-boundary sample point (ignoring the candidate's own unit-radius extent) routinely triggered host-exterior rejections -- fixed by aiming at the sample pulled inward by one unit radius; (5) parent selection ignored height, so a parent already at/above the target's height could never validly reach it under rule 5's positive-rise requirement -- fixed by preferring parents at/below the target's height; (6) the target-attempt and global-plateau stuck counters originally counted successful-but-not-yet-covering steps as stagnation, abandoning/plateauing runs on targets that were still making real progress -- fixed to count only consecutive rejections, plus a separate distance-based stagnation check for the different failure mode of many accepted steps not actually closing the gap (observed directly: one target held 700+ consecutive acceptances without ever being covered or abandoned). Performance: the fixed algorithm initially took ~140s for a full 3-candidate generateCandidates() call at box/default-50%-target (buildCandidateMesh's marching-tetrahedra pass over an 800+-unit smooth-min field was the dominant cost at 25-44s/candidate, freezing the tab's main thread the whole time, confirmed by the browser automation tool itself timing out against an unresponsive page) -- cut COLONIZATION_BUDGET_SAFETY_FACTOR (4->1.5) and COLONIZATION_BUDGET_HARD_CAP (1500->500) to bring it to ~31s total, an explicit documented speed/coverage trade-off. HONEST RESULT after all fixes: field-only reaches roughly 5-11% measured surface coverage against the 50% default target before exhausting its budget (and visibly spreads across most of the host's footprint rather than staying a single pillar -- the plan doc's own §10 qualitative bar); coin/ring-constrained reach roughly 1-5% -- support-angle-constrained lateral reach is genuinely hard under this Study's simplified greedy approach (no §4.1 multi-term score, no §4.2 frontier/spatial-hash search), and this gap is reported honestly via coverageGap/coverageStopReason rather than hidden -- never asserted as target-reached when it wasn't (verified by dedicated growth.test.ts cases). UI: new '造形表現 -- Target surface occupancy' section (own section, separate from printer settings per the plan doc's 'creative parameter, not a printer setting' framing) with 25/50/75%/Custom buttons (default 50%); always-visible target%/measured%/gap%/stop-reason row; detailed metric table gained covered/uncovered/unreachable sample counts and probe depth. renderer.ts gained a toggleable (default off) coverage-sample overlay (green=covered/dark-gray=uncovered, small markers per the plan doc's 'must not obscure the form' requirement) -- the plan doc's 'current target' (yellow) highlight is NOT rendered, an honest scope decision since it's transient generator-loop state not part of the persisted GrowthResult and this Study doesn't animate generation step-by-step. Automated tests: growth.test.ts grew from 36 to 50 assertions (7 new S1 coverage-measurement tests -- reference-sample determinism/area-weight-sum/empty-coverage/near-full-coverage-fixture/ring-hole-exclusion-including-a-regression-test-for-the-under-counting-bug/unreachable-unit-exclusion/reachable-vs-unreachable-array-order-regression; 7 new S2 growth-behavior tests covering plan doc §8 items 7-13 -- monotonic coverage vs target, target-reached-within-tolerance, seed determinism of the S2 result, Phase A invariance regardless of S2 intensity, full post-colonization reachability, an impossible-strict-angle honest non-success case, and a default-target honest-gap case). Real-browser verification (localhost:5174/interior-growth.html, real coordinate clicks computed from getBoundingClientRect + screenshot/window ratio, window.__interiorGrowth read-only, numeric state cross-checked against the rendered metric table, not screenshots alone): default 50% target 3-candidate generation completed in ~35s with metric-table values matching state exactly; coverage-sample toggle verified via a real click showing green/dark-gray dots correctly; Custom target input reveal/hide verified via a real click; console error-free throughout. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean for every file this round touched (the pre-existing measureS1.ts error, from the other agent's own file, was left as-is -- not mine to fix); `npx vite build` succeeded (9 pages). Did NOT implement S3 (ring distribution modes) or S4 (Fabrication Plan/partitioning) -- explicitly future stages per the plan doc's own §7 staging. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

Stage 1A.1 author-feedback revision (Optimizer/docs/sonnet-instruction-20260724-katachi-interior-growth-author-feedback.md): three author comments after directly trying the Phase 1A screen -- (1) wanted a printer/build-volume preset to reason about scale, (2) layer height + support threshold angle are the only two numbers that felt like real inputs, lateral/span mm values did not, (3) default growth was too shallow to visually evaluate the shape (needed bottom-to-top). Added PrinterPreset (bambu-a1 256mm/bambu-a1-mini 180mm, both official-spec-confirmed 2026-07-24, plus author-editable custom) and fitHostToBuildVolume (uniform contain-fit into 90% of build volume per axis, 10% called out in-UI as Katachi's own assumed margin, never a manufacturer figure) replacing the old typed targetLongestMm entirely. Redefined FabricationEnvelope around layerHeightMm + supportThresholdAngleDeg (author inputs) + a read-only derivedMaxLateralAdvancePerLayerMm recomputed via layerHeightMm/tan(angle) on every change (0/90/non-finite angles rejected); maxUnsupportedSpanMm removed from the envelope entirely, rule 6 now derives its limit from unitRadius*UNSUPPORTED_SPAN_FACTOR(3.0, documented guess) instead of an author mm value. Main screen reordered to Printer -> Host shape -> Layer height -> Support threshold angle -> Generate; every other Phase-1A control (seed, GrowthParams sliders, root目標数, build axis) moved into a closed-by-default '研究用詳細' <details>, not deleted. Rebuilt growth as two phases: Phase A grows ONE continuous primary path from a build-plate root toward the host's top via deterministic DFS-with-backtracking (14 azimuthal heading candidates per node, kind-dependent base tilt from buildAxis -- coin 4 degrees since it has no angle rule to satisfy, ring 28 degrees to clear its own MIN_RING_TILT_RAD 20-degree horizontal-rejection with margin -- picked empirically, see below); primaryPathUnitIds/heightCoverage/topReached are captured ONCE right after Phase A and never touched by Phase B's existing BFS branch/fill (verified by a dedicated growth.test.ts case running branching=0.05 vs 0.95 on the same seed and asserting byte-identical primary-path/coverage/topReached). maxUnits removed from GrowthParams entirely; computeAutoBudget derives minimumPathUnits from host-height/step+a 20-unit safety margin, plus a 3x branch budget on top (both 仮決め, documented) -- author input never reintroduced even in the research-details fold, per the instruction's explicit 'author input からは外す' for this one field. heightCoverage = clamp01((maxAcceptedProjection-buildPlateProjection)/(hostTopProjection-buildPlateProjection)), topReached = coverage>=0.95, both shown per-candidate in a new always-visible summary table (accepted/rejected/heightCoverage/topReached) above the collapsible detailed metric table (which also gained primaryPathLength/autoBudget rows). renderer.ts gained a build-volume wireframe box (sized from buildVolumeMm/scaleMmPerUnit, seated exactly on the build plate), a translucent top-reached-threshold plane (opacity reflects topReached), and lowest/highest growth-point markers. history.ts's parseRecipe now detects and migrates legacy Phase-1A envelopes (structural detection: presence of the old nullable maxLateralAdvancePerLayerMm/maxUnsupportedSpanMm keys, absence of supportThresholdAngleDeg) -- a real non-null old lateral value is inverted exactly via atan(layerHeight/lateral) to recover the equivalent angle, a null (unset) old envelope maps to the new defaults (30deg/0.2mm); the old setTargetLongestMm op is dropped (no equivalent concept under the printer-preset model); stored GrowthResult snapshots inside old generateCandidates ops get the same envelope migration plus honest zero/false/empty backfill for the new primaryPathUnitIds/heightCoverage/topReached/autoBudget fields the old shape never had; legacyMigrated is surfaced in both the UI status line and saved provenance. Real-browser verification (isolated Chrome, real coordinate clicks/PointerEvents/form_input, window.__interiorGrowth used read-only) found and fixed one real bug DURING this round: onLayerHeightChange/onSupportThresholdAngleChange (main.ts) updated layerHeightMm/supportThresholdAngleDeg on the envelope but never recomputed derivedMaxLateralAdvancePerLayerMm, so rule 5 kept using a stale derived value after any edit -- caught by directly reading window.__interiorGrowth.getState().envelope after a real form_input edit and seeing the derived number not change; fixed by having both callbacks call computeDerivedLateralAllowance inline. Also tuned two growth-density issues found via growth.test.ts's new height-coverage assertions: sphere+coin-constrained initially landed at heightCoverage 0.945-0.948 (just under the 0.95 bar) -- root-plate-contact tolerance (evaluateCandidate's plateTolerance) was too tight for a curved host's shrinking near-pole footprint (maxR*0.6 -> maxR*2.0, plateBand pre-filter widened unitRadius*2.5 -> *4 to match), and the primary-path tilt was uniformly 35 degrees for every kind even though coin has no angle rule at all, wasting step length as unnecessary lateral drift -- split into PRIMARY_PATH_TILT_RAD_COIN(4deg)/_RING(28deg); after both fixes box/sphere/waisted all reach topReached=true across all 3 variants (heightCoverage 0.978-0.994) at default Printer=A1-mini/Host=box/LayerHeight=0.2/Angle=30 settings, verified both by growth.test.ts (36 assertions total, up from 19) and by a real-browser generate showing all three panels as a continuous root-to-top column crossing the green top-reached plane with a red highest-point marker at the tip -- confirmed by the numeric heightCoverage/topReached fields as well as the screenshot, not screenshot alone (per the instruction's explicit 'スクリーンショットだけで断定せず' requirement). Also verified: printer switch updates build-volume/host-bbox text and clears stale results (existing invalidation pattern); Custom preset's X/Y/Z inputs appear only when Custom is selected and drive a real build-volume fit; STL/provenance save succeeds after a printer switch + regenerate; angle raised to 60deg (derived lateral 0.231mm/layer) still reaches topReached on all 3 candidates; all 8 existing pages remain console-error-free. npm run build (9 pages), growth.test.ts (36/36), npm run test:partition (62/62, no regression), git diff --check (both repos) all passed. Did not implement real CoinSRF/real STL hosts, N-partition, load-path proxy, or FEM -- explicitly out of scope per the instruction's own §1 exclusion list. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

T1 initial implementation (Phase 0/1A, docs/sonnet-instruction-20260724-katachi-interior-growth-stage1.md): new self-contained Study. Host = 3 pure synthetic SDF fixtures (box/sphere/waisted, hostSdf<0=inside, sign-correct approximations not exact distance fields). GrowthField (field.ts's growthDirection) is a pure deterministic function of position only (lift/drift/cohesion), not copied from Kumo. growth.ts's growNetwork BFS-grows coin/ring units from build-plate roots, applying 6 support-constraint rules (host containment w/ small clip tolerance, root-plate contact, parent-field overlap, lateral-advance-vs-layer-height, unsupported-span estimate, plus ring-specific horizontal-axis and node-continuity rejections) only when constraintsActive (field-only variant applies rule 1 alone). Void/reachability analysis via grid flood-fill (analyzeVoids/sampleVoidCellCenters) classifies solid/closed-void/exterior-connected-void, never conflating exterior-connectivity with support-removability. meshExport.ts reuses cloud-sculpt/meshExport.ts's buildMeshFromField/rescaleMeshResult/orientMeshForSavedStl/inspectSavedStlTopology unchanged (canonical scale derived once from host bounds, shared by all 3 candidates, per the gate-correction precedent skin's A/B partition established). renderer.ts uses ONE shared THREE.PerspectiveCamera+OrbitControls rendered into 3 scissored viewports on one canvas (not 3 synced cameras) so 'same camera/same scale' holds by construction; InstancedMesh beads (not raymarch) for accepted/rejected/void display. Real-browser verification (isolated Chrome port 5185, real coordinate clicks/PointerEvents, no synthetic element.click()) found and fixed 3 real bugs: (1) STEP_FACTOR=1.7 (ungrounded initial guess) meant coin/ring children never geometrically touched their parent (rule 4 'no-parent-contact' rejected ~100% of child attempts, constrained variants produced accepted=root-count with 0 edges) -- recalibrated to 0.5 by deriving the actual contact threshold from each shape's own point geometry (coin anchor-anchor: step<=1.1*unitRadius; ring node-node: step<=0.56*unitRadius, stricter still under phase misalignment). (2) unitsMesh (THREE.InstancedMesh) was being frustum-culled as a whole because its default bounding sphere is the GEOMETRY's own (radius 1 at local origin), never grown to cover where setMatrixAt-positioned instances actually sit -- verified via a debug handle (window.__interiorGrowth) that instance count/position/color were all correct despite zero visible beads; fixed with unitsMesh.frustumCulled=false. (3) main.ts originally wrapped the panel in an extra unstyled 'panelHost' div between #app and .panel, breaking the flex-stretch+overflow-y:auto scroll every other Study's #viewport+.panel sibling structure relies on -- the unconstrained wrapper let .panel grow to its full content height, and the overflow silently escaped into #app's own (hidden but still programmatically scrollable via scrollIntoView) box, pushing the canvas off-screen; fixed by making .panel a direct child of #app (mountUi() now tracks and replaces the panel root directly, no wrapper). After all 3 fixes: full walkthrough (host select -> envelope input -> GrowthParams -> 3-candidate generate -> rejected/void toggle -> metric table -> STL/provenance save -> recipe export -> host switch to waisted/sphere) verified with real coordinate clicks, box host at default params: Field only 400/400 accepted (unit cap reached) with 395 edges, Coin constrained 400 accepted/395 edges, Ring constrained only 4 accepted/1 edge (ring-horizontal + root-not-on-plate rejections dominate -- a real, honestly-recorded finding that ring's geometric contact constraints are far stricter than coin's at these defaults, left as an open Next item, not a bug). All 3 candidates passed the saved-topology gate (watertight, 0 boundary/non-manifold edges). Optimizer 0.8.2 --quick diagnosed all 3 saved STLs independently (scale=1.0): all watertight, 0% internal overhang (does NOT mean support-free -- unit-to-unit joints aren't distinguished from external surface by Optimizer's visibility rays), external overhang 21.09%/17.26%/14.36%, ring-constrained's estimated min wall thickness (0.153mm) flagged as likely unprintable standalone (a wall-thickness finding, not a support finding, kept separate). All 8 existing pages (index/gravity/sag/mpm/foam/rings/pack/skin) verified console-error-free after adding one nav link each. growth.test.ts (19 assertions, tsx, covering seed determinism/parent validity/reachability/floating-root rejection/host-exterior rejection+clip/constrained-without-envelope refusal/lateral-advance rejection/unsupported-span rejection/horizontal-ring rejection/closed-vs-exterior-void classification via a deterministically constructed 1-cell shell/recipe round-trip/saved-topology gate/SHA-256/input immutability), npm run build (9 pages), npm run test:partition (62 existing tests, no regression), git diff --check (both repos) all passed. Did not proceed to real CoinSRF/real STL hosts, N-partition, join geometry, load-path proxy, or FEM -- explicitly out of scope for Phase 0/1A per the instruction. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

O2 Connected Base + Multi-source Upward Colonization (Optimizer/docs/opus-instruction-20260725-katachi-interior-growth-connected-multisource.md). Independent O1 diagnosis first: reproduced the 2.85/6.40/6.98% baseline, then classified every accepted unit by job and measured ideal-placement yield -- surface-spread was 4-14x more productive per unit than any other role while getting 16-20% of the budget, host-exterior was the largest rejection reason on all three hosts because spread built its headings around the BUILD AXIS rather than the local surface, and the documented plate-connected base had never produced a single unit (it is forbidden by rule 5, since a step along the plate is ~90deg from the build axis). Adopted a hybrid of the instruction's hypothesis and that measurement: rule 2b exempts plate-supported units from the overhang rules (which is what makes a connected base possible at all), spread now builds the real local tangent plane from the nearest reference sample's normal and holds the coverage probe depth as a setpoint, region cost is an estimated unit count with a surface-traversability term, and the budget formula uses the measured per-unit yield instead of pi*r^2. Coin-constrained target-25% gate MET on all three hosts (23.05/23.02/23.00%, all target-reached, 1 graph root, 94-110 plate contacts, saved mesh 1 component, save gate passes). Field evaluation moved to a spatial index (~10x faster per unit, export resolution unchanged at 64) and generation moved into growth.worker.ts with progress/cancel/stale-result discard -- verified in the real browser with hit-tested real-coordinate clicks: main thread answered in 0ms mid-run. Worker did NOT make it faster (24.4s compute, same order as before); only responsiveness changed. Unresolved and recorded: ring-constrained still exports as 18-27 mesh components on box/waisted and is correctly refused by the save gate (material union IS connected, and it is not resolution or the spatial index -- ruled out by measurement); aligning the mesh field with coverage's capsule model did fix sphere ring.

O2 audit-fix P2 only: plate-contact metric meaning separation (Optimizer/docs/opus-correction-20260725-katachi-interior-growth-worker-state-and-plate-metrics.md §2). No growth-algorithm change whatsoever -- coverage budget, score weights, spread/base/trunk constants, field sampler, mesh resolution and every acceptance rule are byte-identical, and the coin/target-25% matrix re-measured exactly at box 23.05% / sphere 23.02% / waisted 23.00% with rootCount 1 on all three. What was wrong: the old GrowthResult.plateContactCount was computed BEFORE growConnectedMultiSource built the connected base (so it read 2 on all three coin hosts), and the 110/96/94 the README and the UI row 'graph root / plate contact' showed was actually coverageResult.launchPointCount -- a coarse CENTROID-based near-plate candidate set whose tolerance came from the unit's own radius, inside which an independent audit measured positive gaps up to 3.630mm (box) / 5.922mm (sphere) / 3.322mm (waisted). Fixed by deleting plateContactCount outright (never reusing the ambiguous name), renaming the helper isUnitPlateContacting -> isUnitNearPlate with its coarseness stated in its own doc, and adding a real material-based measurement: unitLowestMaterialField (min over unitFieldElements' endpoints of projection-radius; exact for a tapered capsule since it is the convex hull of its two end spheres), unitPlateClearanceMm (canonical-scale mm, signed), isUnitOnPlate (tolerance from layerHeightMm, NOT unit radius) and countActualPlateContacts, the last called AFTER every growth stage. Measured actualPlateContactCount at the default coin/target-25% conditions: box 128, sphere 98, waisted 101, against launch candidates 110/96/94. Base-unit clearance range (negative = at or below the plate plane): box -2.938..-0.154mm, sphere -2.381..+0.047mm, waisted -2.276..-0.108mm -- all within one 0.2mm layer at the top end, so the connected-base principle itself still stands; what was broken was the metric's definition, its measurement point and its display name. UI now shows three separate rows (graph root / actual plate contact / region launch candidate), history.ts backfills actualPlateContactCount to null (never 0) for stored results that predate it, and provenance gained two limits entries saying near-plate candidates are not verified contacts and that a measured contact is not a claim about real-machine adhesion. Honest side-finding recorded in the README: this round's re-measure of waisted/ring came out 19.10% / 561 units against the table's 19.43% / 542 (deterministic, same seed and conditions; box ring and sphere ring match exactly) -- cause unidentified, number left unchanged rather than quietly reconciled. npx tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build emits 9 pages. test:interior-growth NOT run (growth.test.ts was being edited concurrently by another session). Not committed; not staged; not pushed; not deployed.

O2 audit-fix P1: generation-context guard for the Worker handshake (Optimizer/docs/opus-correction-20260725-katachi-interior-growth-worker-state-and-plate-metrics.md §1). Root cause: results were guarded by requestId alone, which distinguishes one RUN from another but says nothing about the CONDITIONS it started under -- so changing host mid-run left the run alive and its box results (accepted 1513 = 530+436+547) landed in the sphere state (whose own default is 1399), meshes and save gates included. Fixed with two independent guards, both required: (A) every callback that changes a generation input calls invalidateActiveRun() BEFORE recording the new value, terminating the Worker so a superseded run stops computing (printer preset, custom build volume, host, build axis, layer height, support angle, target coverage, GrowthParams, seed, unit kind, clear, recipe import); (B) a deterministic context key (new generationContext.ts, testable without a DOM) is snapshotted at request time and re-compared at result acceptance, dropping the whole message on any mismatch so state.results/meshCache/provenanceCache/renderer/save gate/history are never written -- never written-then-cleaned-up. Provenance now builds from the request snapshot rather than live state. P2.3 independent-audit correction (2026-07-27, diagnosis-only, NO production behavior change). The PREVIOUS P2.3 revisit's conclusion is RETRACTED to a hypothesis and then re-established only in part -- that earlier note is kept unedited as the record of what was believed at the time, but two of its claims were not proven by the evidence it cited. (1) 'the pieces are not any unit's material' rested on evaluating the hard union at the pieces' SURFACE VERTICES. A smooth-min isosurface always lies outside the hard union's isosurface (blended <= hard everywhere; measured: 0 of 8000 lattice points had blended > hard on all three hosts), so a component FULL of hard material can still have every surface vertex outside it. Proven with a synthetic regression exhibit: two hard spheres (r=0.6, gap 0.2) fused at blendK 2.0 give 0 of 23160 surface vertices inside the hard union (min hard SDF at any vertex +0.0399), while the volumetric measurement finds 128 hard-negative cells (0.615mm3) at N=16 and 856 (0.989mm3) at N=26, converging toward the true 1.81mm3. A genuine blend-only lobe returns the SAME 0.0% under the old criterion -- identical output for opposite cases. (2) 'signed volumes are all POSITIVE, so they are solid pieces, not enclosed-void walls' was measuring orientMeshForSavedStl, not the shape: that step (the last in buildCandidateMesh) flips any component with negative signed volume, and a cavity inner wall and a reversed shell share a sign anyway, so the sign never distinguishes solid from void. Measured: outward shell +8mm3, reversed -8mm3, cavity wall -1mm3, outer+cavity +7mm3; the same satellites read negative in the stage meshes (box exact rank 1 -513.643mm3) and positive in the saved mesh (+495.888mm3). RE-MEASURED BY VOLUME (component closedness/winding checked first, own bbox tiled at a fixed cells-per-longest-edge, inside/outside via the shared lib/geometry/pointInMesh buildInsideTester over that component's triangles only, hard union split into hard<-eps / |hard|<=eps / hard>+eps with eps = half the cell diagonal and the ambiguous band excluded from the verdict, two grid densities per component): 15 non-largest components (box 9, sphere 2, waisted 4) have 0 hard-negative inside cells at BOTH densities and are now blend-only lobes on volumetric evidence; 0 components contain hard material; 4 are UNDETERMINED -- the three hosts' largest components (100% of inside cells fall in the ambiguous band at these densities because the cell is ~5-8mm against a deepest interior hard SDF of only about -3.5mm; needs N>=100 per edge) and box rank 1 in the EXACT post-clip field (0 hard-negative at N=20 but 1 cell / 0.090mm3 at N=32, densities disagree; its saved-mesh counterpart's minimum interior hard SDF is negative though within eps -- box's largest satellite sits ON the hard boundary and cannot be called blend-only). ALSO CORRECTED: 'the plate clip severs nothing' does not follow from pre/post component COUNTS (an intersection can split one component and delete another, preserving the total); measuring component IDENTITY instead (geometry hash of the distinct Float32-mm coordinate set + bbox + signed/absolute volume + build-axis range + plate contact) shows the count preserved on every host while identity is NOT -- but the change is confined to the largest component (box -1768 triangles / -13345.3mm3 / axis-min +4.530mm) and every satellite survives byte-identical, with nothing appearing or disappearing. THE ACTUAL FINDING: the extra components are not detached pieces but the walls of ENCLOSED VOIDS. Classified by signed volume taken BEFORE orientMeshForSavedStl (the only stage where the sign means anything, per the P2.3 audit correction) and independently re-measured by the lead: exactly ONE outward solid boundary per host per field -- hard union box 1 positive / 26 negative, sphere 1/11, waisted 1/19; and the CURRENT PRODUCTION smooth saved mesh box 1 positive / 9 negative, sphere 1/2, waisted 1/4. So the ring-constrained saved mesh has been ONE connected solid all along, and computeConnectedComponentsWithKey -- which the save gate reads -- counts SURFACE shells, conflating 'one piece' with 'no enclosed voids'; a finer grid resolves more small pockets, which is exactly why the count rises with resolution while everything else converges.
